ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The diagram shows a staircase made from congruent rectangles, with 4 horizontal rows. From bottom to top, the rows contain 5, 4, 3, and 2 rectangles. The bottom width of the whole shape is labeled 10 cm, and the total height is labeled 6 cm. A triangle has its base along the full 10 cm bottom and its top vertex at the top center of the rectangle stack. The grey shading is exactly the parts of the rectangles lying outside this triangle. Since the bottom row has 5 congruent rectangles across a total width of 10 cm, each rectangle is 10 ÷ 5 = 2 cm wide. Since there are 4 equal-height rows across a total height of 6 cm, each rectangle is 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 cm high. So each rectangle has area 2 × 1.5 = 3 cm². There are 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 14 rectangles, so the total area of all rectangles is 14 × 3 = 42 cm². The triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 cm, so its area is (1/2) × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². The grey area is the rectangle-stack area outside the triangle, so it is 42 − 30 = 12 cm².

The whole bottom width is labeled 10 cm, and the full height from base to top is labeled 6 cm. Since the bottom row has 5 congruent rectangles, each rectangle is 10/5 = 2 cm wide; since there are 4 equal-height rows, each rectangle is 6/4 = 1.5 cm high. Thus each rectangle has area 2 × 1.5 = 3 cm², and the total area of all rectangles is (5+4+3+2) × 3 = 42 cm². The triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 cm, so its area is 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². The grey region is exactly the part of the rectangle-stack outside the triangle, so subtract: 42 − 30 = 12 cm².
